metaData.title: Fintech Engineering Handbook
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This handbook provides a comprehensive set of engineering patterns for building trustworthy financial systems, covering money representation, ledger recording, and execution flows.
metaData.summary: The Fintech Engineering Handbook is a living document aimed at software engineers building systems where money is the primary focus. It is structured around three core principles: no invented data, no lost data, and no trust. The handbook begins with representing money, covering precision handling (floating-point, arbitrary precision, minor-units, rational numbers), rounding strategies, currency handling (packaging amount and currency, no cross-currency arithmetic, controlled currency set), and FX rates (directionality, time, transactional vs reference rates). It then moves to recording money via the ledger, explaining double-entry bookkeeping, distinction between value time, booking time, and settlement time, audit trails, event sourcing, immutability, reversals and corrections, and GDPR considerations. Finally, it introduces executing money flows with invariants. The content is practical, with clear trade-offs and principles touched for each pattern.

mainPoints.point: Money representation must use precise types; floating-point is almost never acceptable.
mainPoints.explanation: The handbook details four approaches: floating-point, arbitrary precision (BigDecimal), minor-units integer (e.g., cents, satoshis), and rational numbers, emphasizing that storage and computation can combine different methods.

mainPoints.point: Rounding is a business decision with legal implications and must be explicit, conservative, and minimized.
mainPoints.explanation: Rounding should occur only at boundaries like persistence or display, and residuals must be tracked to avoid creating or losing money.

mainPoints.point: Double-entry bookkeeping ensures money is never created or destroyed; balance is derived from movements.
mainPoints.explanation: Every transaction moves money between accounts (credit/debit), and the books always balance. External providers have dedicated accounts. Corrections are made via compensating entries, never by editing the original.

mainPoints.point: Audit trails require immutable, append-only logs with full context: what, when, who, and why.
mainPoints.explanation: Event sourcing is the most principled approach, but comes with complexity. For non-money domains, a conventional model with reliable change logging may suffice.

mainPoints.point: GDPR erasure can be reconciled with immutable ledgers by separating PII from financial data and using crypto-shredding.
mainPoints.explanation: Financial records are largely exempt; PII can be stored in mutable stores keyed by opaque IDs, and encryption key deletion achieves erasure without rewriting history.

keyQuotes: Money can't be created out of nowhere, so we can't tolerate duplicates or arbitrary balance updates.
No trust. Trust neither external providers, internal components, nor the world.
Rounding breaks sums. If a number is split into parts and rounding is applied, the sum of the parts might no longer equal the original number.

relatedArticles.title: Dario Amodei — Policy on the AI Exponential
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Dario Amodei argues that AI is advancing exponentially, creating a dangerous mismatch with slow-moving policy, and proposes concrete actions across regulation, economics, science, civil liberties, and geopolitics to meet the moment.

relatedArticles.title: Fighting financial crime with Claude Cowork
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Qonto built a secure, enterprise-grade MCP Gateway architecture powered by Claude 4.7 Opus to empower fraud investigators, enabling them to analyze complex financial crime cases from a single, interactive workspace.

relatedArticles.title: Agentic Code Review
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: As AI agents generate code at machine speed, the bottleneck in software engineering has shifted from writing code to reviewing it, making code review the most leveraged skill and requiring a fundamental rethinking of how review is done.

relatedArticles.title: Xiaomi MiMo， Explore and Love
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Xiaomi MiMo and TileRT achieve 1000+ tokens/s inference on a 1-trillion-parameter model using commodity GPUs through extreme model-system codesign, including FP4 quantization and DFlash speculative decoding.

relatedArticles.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI engineers detail a five-month experiment building a production software product with zero manually-written code, using Codex agents to achieve 10x velocity and redefining the engineer's role as system designer and feedback loop architect.

relatedArticles.title: Spring AI Agentic Patterns (Part 7): Session API — Event-Sourced Short-Term Memory with Context Compaction
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the Spring AI Session API, a new event-sourced short-term memory layer for AI agents, featuring turn-safe context compaction, multi-agent branch isolation, and keyword-searchable recall storage.

relatedArticles.title: Software Architecture Guide
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This page from Martin Fowler presents his perspective on software architecture, defining it as the important stuff in system design, and serves as a curated guide to his site's extensive resources on application and enterprise architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Make your own event-sourced agent harness using stream processors — Jonas Templestein， Iterate
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Jonas Templestein from Iterate proposes building AI agent harnesses on a single 'event' abstraction backed by events.iterate.com, where stream processors reduce immutable event histories into agent state and dynamic workers let you deploy logic by just appending JavaScript as an event.

relatedArticles.title: Inside FAISS: Billion-Scale Similarity Search
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep, visual, and intuitive explanation of FAISS, covering the core ideas of IVF, Product Quantization, their combination in IVFPQ, and GPU acceleration, to enable billion-scale similarity search.

relatedArticles.title: Variance: The AI Startup Automating Fraud Detection for Fortune 500s
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Variance is an AI startup founded by ex-Apple engineers that utilizes self-healing AI agents to automate complex fraud detection and compliance for global platforms like GoFundMe.
